prompt: Here's a `WriteService` that runs identically on every replica of a stateless, horizontally-scaled fleet, all writing to one shared database. To stop concurrent writers from clobbering each other, every call to `updateResource` takes a distributed lock before touching the row. Under load we're seeing throughput completely flatline — adding more replicas doesn't help at all, as if there were only one writer in the whole system. Walk me through why that's happening, then tell me how you'd change the locking so that writes to unrelated resources run fully in parallel again, while writes racing on the *same* resource are still safe from lost updates. How would you verify your fix actually restores that parallelism?
